claims.text: The starting material is a consolidated CrMnFeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy containing a minor ZrC addition.
Plasma-transferred-arc-consolidated CrMnFeCoNi with ZrC remains predominantly FCC.
Aging the consolidated alloy at approximately 400 °C for 30 hours will induce in situ precipitation of uniformly distributed nanoscale ZrC particles.
Using an inert atmosphere during aging will avoid oxidation.
The aging temperature and duration can be optimized to produce uniform ZrC precipitation without over-aging.
Nanoscale ZrC particles impede dislocation motion in the FCC matrix.
Nanoscale ZrC particles impede grain-boundary sliding.
Obstruction of dislocation motion by ZrC particles improves yield strength.
Obstruction of dislocation motion and grain-boundary sliding by ZrC particles retards room-temperature creep.
ZrC precipitates modify local electrochemical activity at matrix interfaces.
The interfacial electrochemical effect of ZrC precipitates promotes formation of a stable passivating film.
Formation of a stable passivating film improves resistance to localized or pitting corrosion.
Compared with the untreated ZrC-containing baseline, the aged alloy will have higher yield strength.
Compared with the untreated ZrC-containing baseline, the aged alloy will have higher hardness.
Compared with the untreated ZrC-containing baseline, the aged alloy will have a lower room-temperature creep rate.
Compared with the untreated ZrC-containing baseline, the aged alloy will have lower corrosion current density.
Lower corrosion current density indicates lower corrosion rate and greater corrosion resistance.
Over-aging may produce coarser precipitates that diminish ductility or make the improvements inconsistent.
The proposed improvements should hold under processing conditions similar to plasma transferred arc consolidation followed by controlled inert-atmosphere aging.
